PC: Learner counsels parent on what to do if child gets ill or there is an outbreak in the community given that he is unvaccinated
MK: Learner is aware of common immunization concerns
Learner is able to provide information to refute common immunization concerns
Learner addresses known side effects of vaccines
Learner discusses risks of vaccine preventable diseases
SBP: Learner provides additional resources for parent
Learner makes no plan to re-address issue at future visits
ICS: Learner opens conversation in a non-judgmental and encouraging manner (ie, “your child is due for vaccines and I want to talk about them with you”)
Learner used open ended questions to identify parental concerns
Learner explains their own background and ability respond to immunization questions
Learner restates parental concerns and address them independently
Learner shares a combination of science and anecdotal information about the importance of vaccines
Learner articulates that he/she is available to answer questions in the future and will continue to discuss
Learner opens conversation in a judgmental and negative manner (ie “I hear you don’t want to vaccinate”)
Learner makes assumptions about parental concerns (ie “you don’t have to worry about autism”)
Learner only says that vaccines are “required for school” and “everyone knows they are safe”
PBLI: Learner is unaware of common immunization concerns and seems confused by parent’s questions, fails to offer to research further if needed.
PROF: Learner uses threat (“you will be dismissed from this practice”) to convince parent
